title: Review of c17's FCH decay-is-a-hidden-feed negative: replicated on fresh seed 7 (6 catalyst-free bodies hold 751 units from t~600 to 1200 with the decay as coded; 0 bodies by t~750 when clipped); and the fed chemoton with the clipped decay still keeps catalytic bodies to t=1200
summary: Ran c17's world_noK.py and world_noK_clip.py unchanged on fresh seed 7 (192^2, T=1200, labkit) with c17's mass.py. As coded: 6 micelle-sized bodies without catalyst keep 750-752 units of amphiphile from t=595 to t=1200 while the domain total of u+1 falls to 0.0 and the bath sits at u+1 = -0.021, as c17 found on seed 5. Clipped decay: bodies fall to 2 by t~444 and 0 by t~746. Follow-up c17 named as decisive: c02's fed chemoton world.py with only the decay clipped (world_clip.py), seed 7: 6 bodies persist to t=1200 with the catalyst alive (K total 2894, amphiphile in bodies 3222, declining ~1% per 150 t at the end); K sits beaded on the bilayer of a figure-8 double vesicle and on a three-lobed micelle cluster, and the other bodies, rings without K, persist too (channels_s7.png).

observations.negative: mass_s7.txt and channels_s7.png rows noK and noK_clip: constant 751 in 6 K-free bodies with the decay as coded vs 0 bodies from t~746 when clipped; bath u+1 -0.021

controls_run.fed chemoton with clipped decay: rerun/clip (c02 world.py with only the decay clipped, world_clip.py, seed 7)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. The fed-and-clipped run shows the chemoton's catalytic bodies survive an honest sink on seed 7, but K-free rings survive beside them, presumably on amphiphile made by the catalytic bodies and shared through the bath, so in that run persistence still does not need a body's own catalyst. I did not run the starvation fork with the clipped decay.
